title: Катю зовут на ужин шейха  (Katya Is Summoned to the Sheikh's Dinner)

segments.t: In his office, Barinov answers a frantic phone call from Katya explaining why she let Yulya slip out to the Metropol. Seconds later, a knock sounds on the suite door summoning 'Yulya' to dinner with the sheikh.
Она угрожала рассказать, что я её раздел?
Не знаю, сказала, на часик в «Метрополь» съездит.
Я ей свой мобильник дала на всякий случай.
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
Она угрожала рассказать, что я её раздел?
'She threatened to say that I undressed her?' The '-a' ending on the past-tense verb for 'threatened' marks a female speaker or subject.
'Well, and when will she return?' In Russian, the idea of 'come on' flows naturally into 'will return' without extra filler words. Katya answers right away.
Не знаю, сказала, на часик в «Метрополь» съездит.
'I do not know, she said she would go to the Metropol for an hour.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'not' and finishing on 'will go'.
Я ей свой мобильник дала на всякий случай.
'I gave her my cell phone just in case.' The meaning hinges on 'I' working together with 'case' in spoken Russian.
'Oh, someone is knocking!' An emphatic spoken line centered on the verb meaning 'is knocking'. Chef Barinov answers right away.
'Yulya, it is time for dinner.' Chef Barinov brings out the contrast between 'Yulya' and 'it's time' in a few short words.
'Hello, Dad, I am doomed!' Katya anchors the line on 'hello', while 'end' completes the thought.
'They called me to dinner!' In Russian, the idea of 'me' flows naturally into 'called' without extra filler words. Chef Barinov answers right away.
'Alright, calm down.' Chef Barinov anchors the line on 'so', while 'calm down' completes the thought.
'Find her clothes and put them on.' In Russian, the idea of 'find' flows naturally into 'put on' without extra filler words.
'Dad, I am very scared!' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'dad' and finishing on 'am afraid'. Chef Barinov answers right away.

'Do not be afraid, I will think of something.' In Russian, the idea of 'not' flows naturally into 'will come up with' without extra filler words. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.
Она угрожала рассказать, что я её раздел?
Не знаю, сказала, на часик в «Метрополь» съездит.
Я ей свой мобильник дала на всякий случай.
Dressed from head to toe in Yulya's veil and abaya, Katya is escorted downstairs to sit at the sheikh's dinner table. Until next time!
